566:
(a) Purposes and intent. It is the primary purpose of this article to provide for the reasonable protection of life and property from the hazards created by fire, smoke, explosion, or panic created from a fear of fire or smoke. It is the intent of this article to accomplish its purpose:
(1) Through educational efforts and programs designed to change high-risk attitudes and behaviors that are the root causes of most fire-related problems;
(2) Through consultations and informational programs, develop in people an awareness of the provisions of this article and other applicable laws, and aid them to determine the options available to correct hazards or problems noted; and
(3) By providing through this article reasonable, realistic, and practical safeguards against fire and its related hazards. This article is declared to be remedial and shall be constructed to secure beneficial interests and purposes, which are public safety, health, and general welfare, through safety to life and property from fire, explosion, and other hazards incident to the use and occupancy of buildings, structures or premises.
(b) Scope.
(1) Applicability. The provisions of this article shall apply to all new and existing buildings, structures, premises, facilities, and applicable conditions within the County; however, existing situations or conditions not in strict compliance with this article may be permitted to continue unless they are deemed by the Fire Marshal to constitute a distinct hazard to life or to property from fire, smoke, or explosion. The provisions of this article shall not apply to the interior of one- or two-family dwellings or apartments that are used strictly for residential purposes. This article shall apply to such dwelling units whenever an activity coming under this article is conducted in such units and which creates a hazard from fire, smoke, or explosion to life or to property.
(2) Federal and State authority. The provisions of this article shall not be held to deprive any Federal or State agency or any applicable governing body having jurisdiction of any power or authority which it had on the effective date of the adoption of this article or individual or corporation of its legal rights as provided by law.
(3) Appendices. The appendices included in the codes adopted in section 18-65 are not intended for enforcement unless specifically referenced in the text of such codes.
(4) Referenced standards. Standards referenced in the codes adopted in section 18-65 shall be considered an integral part of such codes without separate adoption. If specific portions of a standard are denoted by code text, only those portions of the standard shall be enforced. Permissive and advisory provisions in a standard shall not be construed as mandatory.
(5) Existing buildings and special historic buildings. The provisions of this article shall apply to existing buildings or structures in the County; however, the provisions of such codes shall be coordinated by the Fire Marshal. The provisions of this article shall apply to special buildings or structures identified by the State or by the County as historic buildings; however, the provisions of this article shall be coordinated by the Fire Marshal with the applicable provisions of applicable State laws or regulations.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.2)
567:
There is created the Bureau of Fire Prevention and Community Emergency Education within the County for the purpose of implementing the provisions of this article. The Bureau shall be under the direction and general supervision of the Fire Marshal. The Fire Marshal is responsible to the Fire Chief for the implementation of the provisions of this article and for the direction and supervision of the Bureau. The Bureau shall strive to improve the safety of the lives and property from fire and associated hazards within the County through programs of safety education through consultations, and through the inspection of buildings, structures, facilities, and premises as often as deemed appropriated by the Fire Marshal. As the Fire Chief and Fire Marshal deem appropriate, the Bureau may develop and implement, in coordination and cooperation with other departments, agencies, or organizations, a comprehensive program of community emergency education.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.3)
568:
The Fire Chief shall recommend the Fire Marshal to the Chairperson, who shall have discretion in appointment of the Fire Marshal. The Fire Marshal shall possess the required qualifications to be deputized by the State Fire Marshal. The Fire Marshal shall serve at the discretion of the Chairperson.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.4)
569:
The Fire Chief may detail or assign members of the Fire Department to the Bureau of Fire Prevention and Community Emergency Education to assist the Fire Marshal. Such members shall be under the direction and supervision of the Fire Marshal during their detail or assignment to the Bureau. The Fire Chief, upon request of the Fire Marshal with approval by the Chairperson, may fill positions deemed necessary for carrying out the purposed and programs of the Bureau, in accordance with the personnel policies and regulations of the County. The selection shall be open to members and nonmembers of the Fire Department. Personnel assigned to fill positions with the bureau shall be under direction and supervision of the Fire Marshal.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.5)
570:
The Sheriff's Department, the Code Official, or other Law Enforcement Officers of the County shall render assistance to the Fire Marshal or the Fire Chief in the implementation and enforcement of this article upon the request of the Fire Marshal or, as appropriate, the Fire Chief.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.6)
571:
The Fire Marshal is authorized to inspect, or to cause to be inspected, as he deems appropriate or necessary based on fire experience in the community, on complaint, or on other applicable grounds, and as resources permit, buildings, structures, premises, and facilities coming within the scope of this article. The purpose of such inspections is to ascertain if any condition exists which could be reasonably construed to cause a fire or explosion or that could contribute to the spread of a fire or its byproducts, or to ascertain any significant non-conformance with purposes, intent, and other provisions of this article or of any other applicable law, rule, or regulation affecting safety to life and/or property from fire, explosions, or related hazards. The Fire Marshal is authorized to apply other applicable laws, and to cause to be corrected any condition which could be reasonably construed to cause a fire or explosion, or that could contribute to the spread of a fire, or any significant non-conformance with the purposes, intent or provisions of this article affecting safety to life and/or property from fire, explosion, or related hazards.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.7)
572:
(a) A copy of the registered architect or engineer plans for all proposed apartment, townhouse, daycare, medical, commercial, institutional, industrial, and other similar type building shall be submitted to the Fire Department for review prior to a building permit being issued.
(b) A copy of the architect or engineer plans for all proposed single-family dwellings that are 5,000 square feet or more shall be submitted to the Fire Department having jurisdiction for review prior to a building permit being issued.
(c) A copy of the registered architect's plans for all proposed buildings that have been submitted to the State of Georgia Fire Marshal's Office for plans review shall also be submitted to the Fire Department for review prior to a building permit being issued.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.8)
573:
The Fire Chief/Fire Marshal or their authorized representatives may, to the extent permitted by law, have free access to and the right to enter at all reasonable times any building, structure, facility, or premises coming under the scope of this article, whether completed or under construction, for the purpose of conducting inspections and otherwise implementing the provisions of this article. Before entering any building, structure, facility, or premises not normally open to the public, except when a fire or other emergency condition exists or has occurred, the Fire Marshal or his representative shall obtain the consent of the occupant, owner, or person in charge at the time. Where consent to enter is refused, the Fire Marshal may seek an order or an administrative search warrant from the Magistrate Court or, if deemed appropriated, from the superior court of Walker County authorizing his entry or that of his representatives for the purposes of conducting the inspection or investigation. The term "emergency condition," for purposes of this section, means any condition or circumstance which the Fire Marshal or Fire Chief judges to constitute an immediate threat or danger to the occupants of the building, structure, facility, or premises or to persons or property exposed to a fire, the hazards associated with fire, explosion, the threat of fire or explosion, or exposed risks from some other hazardous condition or circumstance.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.9)
574:
Any application for or the acceptance of any approval, permit, license, or certificate requested or required pursuant to this article or other applicable law or ordinance of the County or State, constitutes agreement and consent by the person making the application, or accepting the approval, permit, license, or certificate to allow the Fire Marshal or his representatives to enter the building, structure, facility, or premises at any reasonable time to conduct inspections as may be deemed appropriate by the Fire Marshal or as otherwise provided by this article or other applicable ordinances, rules, regulations, or State law.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.10)
575:
(a) Whenever the Fire Chief/Fire Marshal or his designated representatives find any violations of this article or any fire hazard, he is authorized to issue or serve a written notice of the findings of an inspection as set forth in this chapter and to notify the Code Official.
(b) Whenever the Fire Marshal or his designated representatives finds any violations of this article or any fire hazard which is deemed to create a serious or significant potential threat to life in the event of a fire or explosion, he is authorized to issue a written order to correct or abate the violations or hazard. Such order, when issued, shall set forth a reasonable and realistic time frame or date limit for correction, abatement, or compliance. The time frame for correction, abatement, or compliance established by or as directed by the Fire Marshal, or his designated representative, may be reasonable correlated by him to the seriousness or relative degree of hazard, and/or to the complexity of the mean of correction or abatement.
(c) Where deemed necessary due to the potential of risk of life or property, the Fire Marshal may issue a verbal order for the immediate correction or abatement of a violation or fire hazard. This may be followed by a written order or notice of action.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.11)
576:
The Fire Marshal or the Fire Chief shall have the authority to summarily abate any violation of this article or any fire hazard which constitutes an immediate or imminent danger or threat to life in their opinion, and where the following of the provisions for obtaining corrective action or abatement as set forth elsewhere in this article is not practical in their judgment, and therefore assess the abatement costs to the owner as a special tax assessment.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.12)
577:
An unsafe building or structure is any building or structure which is deemed to be structurally unsafe or which is not provided with adequate means of egress, or which is deemed to constitute a serious fire hazard, or which is otherwise deemed dangerous to human life, or which in relation to existing use constitutes a hazard to the safety, health, or welfare of the public by reason of inadequate maintenance, dilapidation, obsolescence, fire damage, disaster damage, vandalism, flood damage, or abandonment, as specified in this article or by any other applicable codes or ordinances in force in the County. Fifteen days after notice/order has been served and no corrective action has been taken by the owner, an action may be filed in court to prosecute the property owner. If correction action is not made 15 days after conviction (unless there is a different special period of time in the Judge's Orders) the building may be locked up or may be removed by the County. Any such abatement action costs will be assessed to the property and its current owner as a special tax assessment, giving the County a property tax lien against the property in order that the County may recover costs associated with its removal. This includes all properties and buildings damaged prior to the adoption of the ordinance from which this article is derived.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.13)
578:
(a) The service of notices or orders issued in connection with this article may be made by the Fire Marshal or his representative upon the owner, occupant, or person in charge of the building, structure, facility, premises, or portion thereof where the hazard or violation was found, or by delivering a copy of the notice or order to any or all of the persons noted. If such person cannot be served by delivery personally as noted, service may be accomplished by affixing a copy of the notice or order in a conspicuous place at or near the entrance of the building, structure, facility, or premises, or by delivering or sending a copy of the notice or order to the known agent of the owner or occupant, or in the event of an absentee owner with no known agent, by sending a copy by certified or registered mail to the owner's last-known residence, business, or post office address.
(b) If the building, structure, facility, or premises is owned by 1 or more persons and is occupied by 1 or more persons under lease or otherwise, the notice or order issued in connection with this section shall apply to the addition to or changes in the building, structure, or premises such as would immediately become real estate and become the property of the owner and not the occupant unless it is otherwise agreed between or among the owner and the occupant.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.14)
579:
(a) Any person who fails to comply with an order of correction or abatement as set forth in this article, or who shall build or act in violation of this article or of any detailed statement of specifications or plans submitted and approved under authority of this article in connection with any approval, certificate, or permit issued under this article, or who shall perform any act deemed to create a serious potential for fire or explosion and for which the issuance of an order to correct or abate is not adequate, and who is found guilty shall be guilty of a violation of this article. A person found guilty under this section shall, for each and every violation and noncompliance respectively, be subject to punishment as provided by this Code. The imposition of penalty for any violation shall not excuse the violation or permit it to continue, and the responsible person shall be required to correct or abate such violation within a time limit as ordered by the court. When not otherwise specified, each 5 days a prohibited condition or violation continues following an order of the court to correct or abate the condition shall constitute a separate offense.
(b) When the Fire Chief or the Fire Marshal determine that violations of this article warrant the filing of charges or action of the court as provided for in subsection (a) of this section, the issuing of a citation of charges and/or summons to appear before the municipal court upon request of the Fire Chief or the Fire Marshal is authorized.
(c) In addition to the filing of charges as specified in subsections (a) and (b) of this section or as a separate remedy at law, the Fire Marshal, or Fire Chief may seek injunctive relief for any fire hazard, violation, or condition that threatens the safety of life based on the provisions of this article or any applicable code or ordinance of the County or of the State.
(d) The application of penalties by the court as provided for in the fee schedule shall not be held to prevent the enforced removal of prohibited conditions or violations.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.15)
580:
It shall be unlawful for any person to use a building, structure, facility, or premises in violation of the provisions of this article where an order has been affixed to the building prohibiting the use of the building under authority of any provision of this article without the approval of the Fire Marshal or his authorized representative or the court.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.16)
581:
(a) The planning, design, and construction of new buildings, structures, facilities, or premises shall be in conformance with the building code, electrical code, gas code, mechanical code, zoning code, and the life safety code, as adopted by the Board of Commissioners; however, where operations, contents, processes, or conditions are not covered by such codes, the applicable provisions of the article shall apply.
(b) Any alterations, additions, or changes required in existing buildings, structures, facilities, or premises because of a change in use, occupancy, exit design, or other reason shall be made in compliance with the codes noted in subsection (a) of this section and as set forth in section 18-65.
(c) The Fire Marshal shall review plans on new construction and/or renovations or alterations of existing buildings so as to ascertain compliance with the codes and standards.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.17)
582:
(a) New construction. The Fire Marshal shall have the authority to consider and approve a modification of any of the applicable codes for new construction with regard to matters relating to fire protection and safety to life in event of fire or related emergencies where the proposed design fire protection system, building use, or construction method involved is unusual or where such involves an unusual hazard, condition or hardship, and the provisions of the codes and standards of force do not clearly or adequately deal with the proposed design, protection system application or design, building use, or construction method, in their judgment. Furthermore, performance base codes can be used if applicable to all County, State, Federal codes approved by the Fire Chief/Fire Marshal.
(b) Alternate materials. It is the intent of this section to allow the use of designs, systems, methods or devices of equivalent or superior quality, strength, fire resistance, effectiveness, durability, and safety to those prescribed by the applicable codes and standards, provided technical documentation, data, or other information or material acceptable to the Fire Marshal and Code Official is submitted for review and such demonstrates to their satisfaction the equivalency of the design, system, method, or device or the intended use. Any modification or alternate safeguard jointly approved by the Fire Marshal and enforcement/Walker County police shall not afford a condition less safe to life and, where appropriate, property, than in their judgment would be provided with compliance with the provisions of applicable codes.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.18)
583:
(a) Existing conditions. The Fire Marshal shall have the authority to grant a variance to the provisions of this article, or of the codes or standards adopted by reference by this article, upon application in writing by the owner and/or occupant of an existing building, structure, facility, or premises, or by his authorized agent, when there are practical difficulties in the way of carrying out the strict letter of this article or the codes or standards adopted by reference by this article or the County. Such modifications or variance may be granted by the Fire Marshal provided in his judgment the spirit, intent, and purposes of this article are observed, the public safety shall be reasonably and practically secured, the modification is in the interest of the community, and substantial justice will be done. The particulars of any variance granted or allowed, and the decision of the Fire Marshal, shall be approved or disapproved by the Board of Commissioners at the next duly scheduled meeting.
(b) Right to appeal. Whenever the Fire Marshal or Fire Chief shall issue an order pursuant to this article, disapprove an application, refuse to grant a permit, refuse to grant a waiver or modification, or when it is claimed that the provisions of this article or the code and standards adopted by reference by this article or the County do not apply or that their true intent and meaning have been misconstrued or wrongly interpreted, the applicant or aggrieved party may appeal from the order of decision of the Fire Marshal or Fire Chief to the Board of Commissioners in writing, to be received by the Board of Commissioners' Office within 30 days after service of the decision is rendered by the Fire Marshal or Fire Chief. Decisions of the Board of Commissioners may only be appealed if and as provided by the Walker County Code. The provisions of the applicable building code relative to time limits, variations and modifications, and decisions as connected with the building shall be applicable to appeals from the Fire Marshal or the Fire Chief relating to this article. Every decision of the Fire Chief/Fire Marshal relative to this article shall be filed in the Office of the Fire Marshal.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.19)
584:
(a) Interference with Fire Officials. It shall be unlawful for any person to interfere with, abuse, or obstruct in any way the Fire Chief, Fire Marshal or their representatives in carrying out any actions in accordance with their official duties as set forth by this article, or by any other applicable local ordinance, or by any law or regulation of the State.
(b) Unlawful use of credentials; unlawful impersonation of Fire Official. It shall be unlawful for any unauthorized person to use an official or unofficial badge or credential so as to impersonate an authorized Fire Official or to otherwise impersonate a Fire Official.
(c) Authority to investigate fires, explosions, false alarms, or related incidents. The Fire Marshal or his authorized representatives are authorized to investigate the cause, origin, and circumstances of any fire or explosion, or to investigate any incident resulting from the sending or sounding of a false alarm of fire or a bomb threat. When in the judgment of the Fire Marshal/Fire Chief reasonable cause exists that a fire or explosion may have been of criminal origin, the Fire Marshal/Fire Chief or their authorized representative is authorized to locate and take custody of any or all physical evidence relating to the cause of the fire or explosion and to continue the investigation to the extent deemed appropriate within the limits of Fire Prevention Bureau resources and within the limits of applicable State laws. The Fire Marshal/Fire Chief shall inform the Sheriff's Department of each fire of criminal or suspected criminal origin, false alarms, or bomb threats. Also, he shall assist the Sheriff's Department in its investigations of reported incidents if so requested by the Department. The Sheriff's Department shall be responsible for the investigation of fires and/or explosions of criminal or suspected criminal origin, false alarms or bomb threats so as to identify, apprehend, and assist in the prosecution of the person responsible for such criminal act.
(d) Evacuation of buildings, structures, facilities, or premises. When in the judgment of the Fire Marshal, the Fire Chief or their authorized representatives in their absence, there is an actual or serious potential danger to the occupants of or persons in close proximity of any building, structure, facility, or premises because of unsafe structural conditions, the presence of explosives, explosive fumes or vapor, toxic fumes, gases or materials, the Fire Marshal, the Fire Chief, or their authorized representatives in their absence, may order the complete or partial immediate evacuation area and shall not reenter until authorized to do so by the official who issued the evacuation order. This section shall not pertain to bomb threats where no bomb or explosive device is known to exist. In such bomb threat situations, the decision to evacuate or not to evacuate is the responsibility of the person in charge of the building, structure, facility, or premises at that time.
(e) Permits and approvals. No person shall maintain, store, or handle materials, or conduct processes which produce conditions hazardous to life or property, or install equipment used in connection with such activities without first obtaining approval, or as appropriate based on the provisions of this article, a permit from the State Fire Marshal. Where conditions or activities are also regulated by a State or Federal agency and a permit, license, or certificate is required by the regulating agency, no local permit is required; however, the approval of the Fire Marshal is required, and he shall have the authority to apply the provisions of this article where a hazardous condition is discovered.
(f) Tests. All equipment required by this article or other applicable codes adopted by the County or by the State shall be maintained in a safe, sound, and operations condition. The Fire Marshal may require tests or test reports as proof of compliance. Required tests are to be made at the expense of the owner or his agent by an approved testing laboratory or other approval agency or firm acceptable to the Fire Marshal.
(g) Authority to expose or stop work. Whenever any construction or installation coming under this article is subject to inspection prior to use and is covered or concealed without having first been inspected, the Fire Marshal/Fire Chief may require by verbal and/or written order that such work be exposed for inspection. The Fire Marshal shall be notified when the installation is ready for inspection within a reasonable period of time. When any construction or installation work is being performed in violation of the plans, specifications, or understandings as approved by the Fire Marshal, a written order may be issued to the responsible party to stop work on that portion of the work which is in violation. The order shall state the nature of the violation. No work shall be continued on that portion until the violation has been corrected.
(h) Administrative liability. Any officer or employee of the County empowered or authorized to administer or act under the provisions of this article or other applicable codes in force in the County or adopted or required by the State, and acting for the County or State in the discharge of his duties, shall not be held liable personally; and he is relieved from all personal liabilities from any damages that may accrue to any person or property as a result of any act required, implied, or permitted, in the discharge of their duties, or as required, implied, or permitted by this article or other applicable codes in force in the County or adopted or required by the State.
(i) County liability. The County shall not be liable for any damage to persons or property resulting from any act or any failure to act in connection with any provision of this article or other applicable codes in force in the County or adopted or required by the State.
(j) Permitting and inspection. The inspection or permitting of any building or plan by any employee of the Division of Fire Prevention of the Fire Department under the requirements of this article shall not be construed in any court as a warranty of the physical condition of such building or the adequacy of such plan. Neither the County nor any employee of the County shall be liable in tort for damages for any defect or hazardous or illegal condition or inadequacy in such building or plan, nor for any failure or any component of such building, which may occur subsequent to such inspection or permitting.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.20)
585:
The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Approved means acceptable to the Fire Marshal, or as appropriate, the Fire Chief of the County. In determining acceptability of installations, equipment, materials, or procedures, the Fire Marshal, or as appropriate the Fire Chief, may base acceptance on compliance with nationally recognized standards. The Fire Marshal, or as appropriate the Fire Chief, may require evidence of proper installation, proper use, or proper procedures. The Fire Marshal or, as appropriate, the Fire Chief, may also refer to listings or labeling practices of recognized testing laboratories, inspection agencies, or other recognized organizations concerned with product evaluations and which are in a position to determine compliance with appropriate standards for the current production of listed items and the satisfactory performance of such equipment or materials in actual usage.
Building code means the building code adopted.
Chief of the Fire Department means the Fire Chief of Walker County Fire Rescue.
Code Official means any Code Official of the County.
Combustible means capable of undergoing combustion.
Electrical code means the electrical code adopted.
Exit discharge means that portion of a means of egress between the termination of an exit and a public way.
Fire hazard means:
(1) Any thing or act which increases or may cause an increase of the hazard or menace of fire to a greater degree than that customarily recognized as normal by persons in the public service regularly engaged in preventing, suppressing, or extinguishing fire;
(2) Any thing or act which may obstruct, delay, hinder, or interfere with the operations of the Fire Department or with the egress of occupants in event of fire;
(3) A condition which will increase the spread or extent of fire; or
(4) A definite condition of materials, rather than the materials themselves, which has the potential to produce a fire cause.
Gas code means the gas code adopted.
Mechanical code means the mechanical code adopted.
Overcrowding means a condition:
(1) When there are more people in the building or portion of the building than is allowed or posted in accordance with the building code, or where applicable, the State safety fire law; or
(2) When in the judgment of the Fire Marshal or his representative a threat to the safety of life exists due to the number of persons sitting or standing so as to obstruct or impede the use of aisles, passages, corridors, exits, or other component or required means of egress.
Sheriff means the Sheriff of Walker County or his deputy.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-3.21)
588:
To ensure, as far as possible, the safety of the citizens and personnel of the County from the possible harmful effects of hazardous materials, the ordinance from which this article is derived is adopted as an amendment to the fire prevention and protection ordinance to ensure that the quantities and types of hazardous chemicals and extremely hazardous substances will be known and regulated within the County to ensure as far as possible the safety of the citizens of the County from the dangers of hazardous materials.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-4.1)
589:
This article is applicable to any facility that is required to prepare or have available material safety data sheets (MSDS) for hazardous chemicals under the Federal Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970 (and subsequent amendments) and all regulations promulgated under that act, and any facility required to submit reports for extremely hazardous substances, as defined in 40 CFR 355, appendix A, and any facility owning, handling, transporting, storing, or in any other manner or method dealing in Class A, B, and C explosives and blasting agents within the County.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-4.2)
590:
(a) The owner or operator of a facility subject to this article shall submit a material safety data sheet and any other required forms to the Fire Safety Division, or the Fire Department.
(b) Forms must be submitted on all hazardous chemicals present at the facility at any 1 time in amounts equal to or greater than 9,000 pounds (or 3,540 kilograms) and for all extremely hazardous substances present at the facility in an amount greater than or equal to 500 pounds (or 227 kilograms which is approximately 55 gallons) or the threshold planning quantity (TPQ), whichever is lower as defined in 40 CFR 355, appendix A, which provisions is incorporated herein.
(1) The owner or operator of a facility that is subject to this part shall submit the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Tier 24 to the Fire and Safety Division, of the Fire Department, on an annual basis beginning on January 1, 2007.
(2) The owner and operator will also be required to submit a material safety data sheet on all hazardous chemicals as designated by title 29 CFR 1910.120, which provisions are incorporated herein.
(3) The term "hazardous chemical" does not apply to the following:
a. Any food, food additive, color additive, or cosmetic regulated by the Food and Drug Administration.
b. Any substance present as a solid in any manufactured item to the extent exposure to the substance does not occur under normal conditions of use.
c. Any substance to the extent it is used for personal, family, or household purposes, or is present in the same form and concentration as a private package for distribution and used by the general public.
d. Any substance to the extent it is used in a research laboratory or a hospital, or other medical facility under the direct supervision of a technically qualified individual.
(c) The facility will be subject to unannounced inspections by the Fire Safety Division of the Fire Department to ensure compliance with the requirements of this chapter.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-4.3)
591:
(a) All locations within the County boundaries that contain hazardous materials must label all containers in conformity with current DOT guidelines.
(b) The NFPA 704 system will also be required to be placed on a readily visible location of facilities to indicate hazardous materials. The above-mentioned plaque must be securely mounted to the side of any truck, wall, construction trailer, etc., and be in place at the location that is readily visible at all times; and be a minimum of at least 48 inches above ground level.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-4.4)
592:
(a) MSDS reporting. Any person other than a government entity who violates any requirement of this article shall be in violation of this chapter.
(b) Inventory reporting. Any person other than a government entity who violates any requirement shall be in violation of this chapter.
(c) Continuing violations. Each day a violation described in subsection (a) or (b) of this section continues shall constitute a separate violation.
(d) Failure to permit. Any person that fails to obtain or maintain a required hazardous materials permit shall be in violation of this article.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-4.5)
593:
(a) All Class A, B, and C explosives and blasting agents must be reported to the Fire Safety Division. A permit will also be required for all explosives either stored or used within the County. A fee in an amount to be determined by the Board of Commissioners from time to time will be required of the entity involved with the above classes of explosives. The fee must be paid prior to issuance of the permit.
(b) All units that store or contain explosives either mobile or fixed must have the proper DOT or NFPA plaques affixed to all 4 sides of the building or vehicle containing explosives.
(c) Violations.
(1) Failure to report regulated explosives is a violation of this article.
(2) Failure to obtain an explosive permit is a violation of this article.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-4.6)
594:
Any person who violates any of the provisions of this article hereby adopted, or fails to comply therewith, shall for each and every violation and noncompliance respectively be guilty of a violation of the Walker County Code, and such violations shall be punishable as a misdemeanor as defined by the State. The imposition of 1 penalty for any violation shall not excuse the violation to continue. The penalty for violation shall be according to section 1-13.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-4.7)
595:
Venue and jurisdiction of any citations issued under this article shall be as designated in section 18-37.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-4.8)
598:
It is the declared purpose of this article to provide for the designation and identification of fire lanes, for the manner, method, and language for the posting of signs; to establish the penalty for violation of this article, to identify and designate the persons who have authority to enforce the article and the limits of such authority, to prohibit parking in the fire lanes; to provide for the method of submitting properties to this article to repeal all ordinances in conflict herein; and for other purposes.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-5.1)
599:
The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Enforcement Officers means any duly authorized Law Enforcement Officer employed by the County.
Fire lanes means areas designated by the Fire Official providing access for Fire Department vehicles to buildings, Fire Department connections, and fire hydrants. The term "fire lane" includes all alleys, driveways or lanes, devoted to public use, where the parking of motor vehicles or other obstructions can interfere with ingress or egress of Fire Department vehicles for the protection of person and properties including, but not limited to, shopping centers, theaters, hospitals, bowling lanes, churches, multifamily housing, and high-rise buildings.
Fire Official means the Fire Officer or other designated authority, or their duly authorized representative, charged with the administration and enforcement of the fire prevention and protection ordinance.
Master plans means all original plans drawn in accordance with this article; all copies distributed shall be from this original drawing.
Needed fire flow means as defined by Insurance Services Office (ISO) fire suppression rating schedule.
New building means any commercial or public facility whose plans were submitted after this amendment goes into effect.
Plats means maps created by the building owner and approved by the Fire Marshal or his designee which depict the location and boundaries of land and all existing fire lanes in accordance with this article. Such maps shall be drawn to scale.
Property owners means each person, firm, corporation, or entity possessing any estate, or leasehold right in the property being designated as fire lanes.
Ticket means an order issued out of court by an Enforcement Officer of the County directing a violator of this article to comply with all civil fines set forth.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-5.2)
600:
(a) Every existing building shall be accessible to Fire Department apparatus by way of access roadways with all-weather driving surfaces of not less than 20 feet (6.1 m) of unobstructed clear width, with adequate roadway turning radius capable to supporting the imposed loads of the fire apparatus and having a minimum vertical clearance of 13 feet 6 inches (4.1 m).
(1) Where fire protection systems approved by the Fire Official are provided, the above-required clearances may be modified by the Fire Official.
(2) The Fire Official shall have the authority to require an increase in the minimum access widths where they are inadequate for fire or rescue operations.
(b) Every new building shall be accessible to Fire Department apparatus by way of designated fire lanes with an all-weather surface of not less than 20 feet (6.1 m) of unobstructed clear width. There shall be a minimum roadway turning radius of 35 feet (10.6 m). There shall be a minimum vertical clearance of 13 feet 6 inches (4.1 m). The designated fire lanes shall be paved, poured concrete, or equivalent, capable of supporting the gross vehicle weight of fire apparatus.
(1) Where fire protection systems approved by the Fire Official are provided, the above-required clearances may be modified by the Fire Official.
(2) The Fire Official shall have the authority to require an increase in the minimum access widths where they are inadequate for fire or rescue operations.
(c) During construction, when combustibles are brought onto the site in such quantities as deemed hazardous by the Fire Official, access roads and a suitable water supply, acceptable to meet the required needed fire flow, shall be provided and maintained.
(d) The areas designated as fire lanes shall have signs posted meeting the following criteria:
(1) Signs shall read "No Parking Fire Lane," be constructed of a material to withstand the elements, such as metal, and lettering shall contrast against the background.
(2) Letters shall not be less than 2 inches in height.
(3) One sign shall be placed at the beginning of the fire lane and 1 at the end of the fire lane and a sign shall be erected every 50 feet of the fire lane.
(4) Signs posted shall not be more than 4 feet from the edge of the curb and shall be visible from both driving directions, regardless of time of day or the driving surfaces.
(e) Painted lines, or equivalent, may be required by the Fire Official for that portion of the fire lane that is located in the parking areas, or is subject to blocking by parked vehicles. Such lines shall be yellow and clearly define an area 20 feet clear width from the building as no parking fire lane.
(f) The Fire Official may require curbs of non-parking areas be painted red or other distinctive colors.
(Ord. of 11-16-2006, § 23-5.3)
601:
All fire lanes shall be approved by the Fire Official pursuant to these regulations, and thereafter these fire lanes shall be maintained by the property owner. Designated fire lanes or roads deemed necessary for Fire Department access by the Fire Official shall be maintained in a passable condition.
(1) Private property owners or their representatives shall be responsible for keeping all fire lanes within the County's jurisdiction free of all obstructions.

(a) Fire Department access roads shall be provided and maintained in accordance with this section.

(a) Purpose. It is the purpose of this section to regulate responsibilities of those persons who purchase, rent, or use alarm systems, devices, or services. This section is also intended to encourage the improvement and reliability of these systems, devices, and services and to ensure that Police and Fire Department personnel will not be unduly diverted from responding from actual criminal activity as a result of responding to false alarms. This section specifically encompasses fire alarms, burglar alarms, robbery alarms, hold-up alarms, medical alarms, and panic alarms, both audible and inaudible (silent). The provisions of this section shall not apply to alarm systems which are owned or maintained by Walker County, with exception of those alarms which are installed by a tenant on premises in which the County merely has a property interest as a landlord.
(b) Definitions. The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this section, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Alarm means and includes any fire, robbery, burglary, hold-up, medical, or panic alarm that transmits any signal (audible, visual, or silent) to the County indicating a pre-determined emergency condition, whether the alarm is received either:
(1) By a telephone line to a designated position on an alarm panel;
(2) By a private alarm service company relayed to the County Communications Center telephone;
(3) By an automated telephone alarm system, playing a recorded message when received on the County Communications Center telephone; or
(4) By a signal relayed to the County Communications Center by a third party.
False alarms means the activation of an alarm system where none of the emergencies for which the alarm system has been installed have in fact occurred.
Response means the dispatch of any law enforcement or fire unit to the premises where an alarm has been activated or the arrival of an officer to the location by any means or notification.
(c) Automatic dialers; automatic response alarm systems. It shall be unlawful to key automatic response alarm systems to any County or Walker County Fire Rescue telephone number. Such alarm shall only be keyed to a private answering service, who can then notify the County Communications Center.

(a) Preliminary research.
(1) Compilation and collection of information and surveys. The Historic Preservation Commission shall compile and collect information and conduct surveys of historic resources within the County. The Historic Preservation Commission, as outlined in article II, division 2 of chapter 2, reviews plans for historic districts and properties.
(2) Power to recommend districts and properties. The Commission shall present to the County Board of Commissioners recommendations for historic districts and properties.
(3) Designation report. Prior to the Commission's recommendation of an historic district or historic property to the County Board of Commissioners for designation, the Commission shall prepare a designation report consisting of:
a. A physical description;
b. A statement of the historical, cultural, architectural and/or aesthetic significance;
c. A map showing district boundaries and classification (i.e., contributing, or non-contributing) of individual properties therein, or showing boundaries of individual historic properties; and
d. Representative photographs.
(b) Historic district designation.
(1) Criteria for selection. An historic district is a geographically definable area which contains buildings, structures, sites, objects and landscape features, or a combination thereof, which:
a. Has special character or special historic/aesthetic value or interest;
b. Represents 1 or more periods, styles or types of architecture typical of 1 or more eras in the history of the County, the State or the region; and
c. Causes such area, by reason of such factors, to constitute a visibly perceptible section of the County.
(2) Boundaries. Boundaries of historic districts shall be included in the separate ordinances designating such districts and shall be shown on the official zoning maps of the County.
(3) Property classifications. Individual properties within historic districts shall be classified as:
a. Contributing (contributes to the district);
b. Non-contributing (does not contribute to the district, as provided for in subsection (b)(1) of this section).
(c) Historic property designation. An historic property is a building, structure, site or object, including the adjacent area necessary for the proper appreciation or use thereof, deemed worthy of preservation by reason of value to the nation, the State or the County for 1 of the following reasons:
(1) It is an outstanding example and representative of its era;
(2) It is 1 of the few remaining examples of a past architectural style or type;
(3) It is associated with an event or person of historic or cultural significance to the County, the State or the region; or
(4) It is a site of natural or aesthetic interest that is continuing to contribute to the cultural or historical development and heritage of the County, the State or the region.
(d) Ordinance adoption requirements.
(1) Applications. Designations may be proposed by the County Board of Commissioners, the Commission, or:
a. Historic districts. An historical society, neighborhood association or group of property owners may apply to the Commission for designation;
b. Historic properties. An historical society, neighborhood association or property owner may apply to the Commission for designation.
(2) Required contents. Any ordinance designating any property or district as historic shall:
a. List each property in a proposed historic district or describe the proposed individual historic property;
b. Set forth the name of the owner of the designated property;
c. Require that a Certificate of Appropriateness be obtained from the Commission prior to any material change in appearance of the designated property; and
d. Require that the property or district be shown on the official zoning maps of the County and kept as a public record to provide notice of such designation.
(3) Public hearing. The Commission and the County Board of Commissioners shall hold a public hearing on any proposed ordinance for the designation of any historic district or property. Notice of the hearing shall be published in at least 3 consecutive issues in the principal newspaper of local circulation, and written notice of the hearing shall be mailed by the Commission to all owners and occupants of such properties. All such notices shall be published or mailed not less than 10 nor more than 20 days prior to the date set for the public hearing. A notice sent via the United States mail to the last known owner of the property shown on the County Tax Digest and a notice sent via attention of the occupant shall constitute legal notification to the owner and occupant under this section.
(4) Historic preservation division notification. No less than 30 days prior to making a recommendation on any ordinance designating a property or district as historic, the Commission must submit the report required in subsection (a)(3) of this section to the Historic Preservation Division of the Department of Natural Resources.
(5) Recommendations. A recommendation to affirm, modify or withdraw the proposed ordinance for designation shall be made by the Commission within 15 days following the public hearing and shall be in the form of a resolution to the County Board of Commissioners.
(6) Action of Commissioner. Following receipt of the Commission's recommendation, the County Board of Commissioners may adopt the ordinance as proposed, may adopt the ordinance with any amendments deemed necessary, or may reject the ordinance.
(7) Adoption notification. Within 30 days following the adoption of the ordinance for designation by the County Board of Commissioners, the owner and occupant of each designated historic property and each individual property located within a designated historic district shall be given written notification of such designation by the County Board of Commissioners. This notice shall inform said owner and occupant of the necessity of obtaining a Certificate of Appropriateness prior to undertaking any material change in appearance of the historic property designated or within the historic district designated. A notice sent via the United States mail to the last known owner of the property shown on the County Tax Digest and a notice sent via United States mail to the address of the property to the attention of the occupant shall constitute legal notification to the owner and occupant under this article.
(8) Notification of other agencies. The Commission shall notify all necessary agencies within the County of the ordinance for designation.
(9) Moratorium. If an ordinance for designation is being considered, the Commission shall have the power to freeze the status of the involved property.
(Code 2005, § 34-144; Ord. of 8-21-2002, § IV)
661:
(a) Generally.
(1) Approval of material change in appearance in historic districts or involving historic properties. After the designation by ordinance of an historic property or an historic district, no material changes in the appearance of such historic property, or of a contributing or non-contributing building, structure, site or object within such historic district shall be made or be permitted to be made by the owner or occupant thereof unless or until an application for a Certificate of Appropriateness has been submitted to and approved by the Commission. A building permit shall not be issued without a Certificate of Appropriateness.
(2) Exemptions. The Department of Transportation and any contractor, including cities and counties, performing work funded by the Department of Transportation are exempt from this section. Local governments are exempt from the requirement of obtaining Certificates of Appropriateness; provided, however, that local governments shall notify the Commission 45 days prior to beginning any undertaking that would otherwise require a Certificate of Appropriateness and allow the Commission an opportunity to comment.
(b) Submission of plans. An application for a Certificate of Appropriateness shall be accompanied by drawings, photographs, plans and documentation required by the Commission.
(c) Interior alterations. In its review of applications for Certificates of Appropriateness, the Commission shall not consider interior arrangement or use having no effect on exterior architectural features.
(d) Technical advice. The Commission shall have the power to seek technical advice from outside its members on any application.
(e) Public hearings, notices and right to be heard.
(1) The Commission shall hold a public hearing at which each proposed Certificate of Appropriateness is discussed. Notice of the hearing shall be published in the principal newspaper of local circulation in the County and written notice of the hearing shall be mailed by the Commission to all owners and occupants of the subject property. The written and published notices shall be provided in the same manner and time frame as notices are provided before a public hearing for rezoning.
(2) The Commission shall give the property owner and/or applicant an opportunity to be heard at the Certificate of Appropriateness hearing.
(f) Commission action.
(1) Certificate approval or denial option. The Commission may approve the application for a Certificate of Appropriateness as proposed, approve the application with any modifications it deems necessary, or deny it.
(2) Issuance of Certificate subject to adverse effect on historical property or district; criteria. The Commission shall approve the application and issue a Certificate of Appropriateness if it finds that the proposed material change(s) in appearance would not have a substantial adverse effect on the aesthetic, historic, architectural or archaeological significance and value of the historic property or the historic district. In making this determination, the Commission shall consider, in addition to any other pertinent factors, the following criteria for each of the following actions:
a. Alterations or new construction. A decision by the Commission approving or denying a Certificate of Appropriateness for alterations or new construction shall be guided by:
1. The Secretary of the Interior's Standards for the Treatment of Historic Properties, along with any published guidelines accompanying the standards; and
2. Local design guidelines adopted by the Commission.
b. Relocation. A decision by the Commission approving or denying a Certificate of Appropriateness for the relocation of a building, structure or object shall be guided by:
1. The historic character and aesthetic interest the building, structure or object contributes to its present setting;
2. Whether there are definite plans for the area to be vacated and what the effect of those plans on the character of the surrounding area will be;
3. Whether the building, structure or object can be moved without significant damage to its physical integrity; and
4. Whether the proposed relocation area is compatible with the historic and architectural character of the building, structure or object.
c. Demolition. A decision by the Commission approving or denying a Certificate of Appropriateness for the demolition of buildings, structures, sites, trees judged to be 50 years old or older, or objects shall be guided by:
1. The historic, scenic, architectural or archaeological significance of the building, structure, site, tree or object;
2. The importance of the building, structure, site, tree or object to the ambiance of a district;
3. The difficulty or the impossibility of reproducing such a building, structure, site, tree or object because of its design, texture, material, detail or unique location;
4. Whether the building, structure, site, tree or object is 1 of the last remaining examples of its kind in the historic district or in the County;
5. Whether there are definite plans for use of the property if the proposed demolition is carried out, and what the effect of those plans on the character of the surrounding area would be;
6. Whether reasonable measures can be taken to save the building, structure, site, tree or object from collapse; and
7. Whether the building, structure, site, tree or object is capable of earning reasonable economic return on its value.
(g) Variances. When, by reason of unusual circumstances, the strict application of any provision of this article would result in exceptional practical difficulty or undue economic hardship upon any owner of a specific property, the Commission, in passing upon applications, shall have the power to vary or modify strict adherence to said provisions, or to interpret the meaning of said provisions so as to relieve such difficulty or hardship, provided such variances, modifications or interpretations shall remain in harmony with the general purpose and intent of said provisions, so that the architectural or historical integrity, or character of the property shall be conserved and substantial justice done. In granting variances, the Commission may impose such reasonable and additional stipulations and conditions as will, in its judgment, best fulfill the purpose of this article. An undue hardship shall not be a situation of the person's own making.
(h) Deadline for approval or rejection.
(1) The Commission shall approve or reject an application for a Certificate of Appropriateness within 45 days after the filing thereof. Evidence of approval shall be by a Certificate of Appropriateness issued by the Commission. Notice of the issuance or denial of a Certificate of Appropriateness shall be sent by United States mail to the applicant and all other persons who have requested such notice in writing filed with the Commission.
(2) Failure of the Commission to act within said 45 days shall constitute approval and no other evidence of approval shall be needed.
(i) Action upon rejection.
(1) In the event the Commission rejects an application, it shall state its reasons for doing so, and shall transmit a record of such actions and reasons, in writing, to the applicant. The Commission may suggest alternative courses of action it thinks proper if it disapproves of the application submitted. The applicant, if he so desires, may make modifications to the plans and may resubmit the application at any time after doing so.
(2) In cases where the application covers a material change in appearance which would require the issuance of a building permit, the rejection of the application for a Certificate of Appropriateness by the Commission shall be binding upon the building inspector or other administrative officer charged with issuing building permits and, in such a case, no building permit shall be issued.
(j) Conformance required.
(1) All work performed pursuant to an issued Certificate of Appropriateness shall conform to the requirements of such Certificate. In the event work is performed not in accordance with such Certificate, the Commission shall issue a cease and desist order and all work shall cease.
(2) The Commission and the County Board of Commissioners shall be authorized to institute any appropriate action or proceeding in a court of competent jurisdiction to prevent any material change in appearance of a designated historic property or historic district, except those changes made in compliance with the provisions of this article or to prevent any illegal act or conduct with respect to such historic property or historic district.
(k) Action upon non-commencement of construction; period of validity; renewal. A Certificate of Appropriateness shall become void unless construction is commenced within 6 months of the date of issuance. Certificates of appropriateness shall be issued for a period of 18 months and are renewable.
(l) Records. The Commission shall keep a public record of all applications for Certificates of Appropriateness, and of all the Commission's proceedings in connection with said applications.
(m) Acquisition of property. The Commission may, where such action is authorized by the County Board of Commissioners and is reasonably necessary or appropriate for the preservation of a significant historic property, enter into negotiations with the owner for the acquisition, by gift, purchase, exchange or otherwise, of the property or any interest therein.
(n) Appeals. Any person adversely affected by any determination made by the Commission relative to the issuance or denial of a Certificate of Appropriateness may appeal such determination to the County Board of Commissioners. Any such appeal must be filed with the County Board of Commissioners within 15 days after the issuance of the determination pursuant to subsection (h)(1) of this section or, in the case of a failure of the Commission to act, within 15 days of the expiration of the 45-day period allowed for the Commission action pursuant to subsection (h)(2) of this section. The County Board of Commissioners may approve, modify or reject the determination made by the Commission if he finds that the Commission abused its discretion in reaching its decision. Appeals from decisions of the County Board of Commissioners may be taken to the superior court of the County in the manner provided by law for appeals from conviction for County ordinance violations.
(Code 2005, § 34-145; Ord. of 8-21-2002, § V)

(a) Ordinary maintenance and repair. (b) Deterioration by neglect. Property owners of historic properties or properties within historic districts shall not allow their buildings to deteriorate by failing to provide ordinary maintenance or repair. Such conditions as broken windows, doors and exterior openings which allow the elements and vermin to enter or the deterioration of a building's structural system shall constitute failure to provide ordinary maintenance or repair.
(2) In the event the Commission determines a failure to provide ordinary maintenance or repair, the Commission will notify the owner of the property and set forth the steps which need to be taken to remedy the situation. The owner of such property will have 30 days in which to do this.
(3) In the event that the condition is not remedied in 30 days, the owner shall be punished as provided in section 22-66 and, at the direction of the County Board of Commissioners, the Commission may perform such maintenance or repair as is necessary to prevent deterioration by neglect. (a) Generally. In the interpretation and application of this article, all provisions shall be liberally construed in favor of the objectives and purposes of the County and deemed neither to limit nor repeal any other powers granted under statute.

Responsibility for interpretation by the Planning Director shall be limited to standards, regulations, and requirements of this article, but shall not be construed as overriding the responsibility given to the Chairperson, Board of Commissioners, Planning Commission or official named in other divisions or sections of this article.
(c) Computation of time. The time within which an act is to be done shall be computed by excluding the first and including the last day. If the last day is a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, that day shall be excluded.
(d) Gender. Words importing the masculine gender shall be construed to include the feminine and neuter.
(e) Number. Words in the singular shall include the plural and words in the plural shall include the singular.
(f) Written orin writing. The term "written" or "in writing" shall be construed to include any representation of words, letters or agreements, whether by printing or otherwise.
(g) Year and day. The term "year" means a calendar year, unless otherwise indicated, and the term "day" means a working day, unless a calendar day is indicated.
(h) Headings. The headings of this article are intended only for convenience in identifying its various provisions, and shall not affect the substance of the article or any provisions thereof.
(i) Non-technical and technical terms. The ordinary signification shall be applied to all words, except words of art or words connected with a particular trade or subject matter, which shall have the signification attached to them by experts in such trade or with reference to such subject matter.
(j) Boundaries. Interpretations regarding boundaries of land use districts shall be made in accordance with the following:
(1) Boundaries shown as following or approximately following any street shall be construed as following the centerline of the street.
(2) Boundaries shown as following or approximately following any plotted lot line or other property line shall be construed as following such line.
(3) Boundaries shown as following or approximately following section lines, half section lines or quadrant section lines shall be construed as following such line.
(4) Boundaries shown as following or approximately following natural features shall be construed as following such features.
(5) Where a district boundary line, as appearing on the zoning map, divides a lot in single ownership at the time of enactment, the district requirements for the least restricted portion of such lot shall be deemed to apply to the whole thereof, provided that such extensions shall not include any part of such a lot more than 200 feet beyond the district boundary line, so long as this use does not infringe on the buffer as otherwise provided in this article.
(k) Repeal of prior provisions. Any ordinances and provisions in conflict with these regulations are hereby repealed as of the effective date of the ordinance from which this article is derived.
(l) Robert's Rules of Order. On all procedural matters, the County Planning Commission shall follow Robert's Rules of Order.
